  "summary": "Apache Log4j2 JNDI features do not protect against attacker-controlled LDAP and other JNDI related endpoints. An attacker who can control log messages or log message parameters can execute arbitrary code loaded from LDAP servers when message lookup substitution is enabled.",
  "affected_products": [
    "Apache Log4j2 versions 2.0-beta9 to 2.14.1"
  ],
  "cvss_score": 10.0,
  "severity": "CRITICAL",
  "mitigation": "Upgrade to Apache Log4j 2.15.0 or higher (ideally 2.17.1 or newer). For versions 2.10 to 2.14.1, the vulnerability can be mitigated by setting the system property 'log4j2.formatMsgNoLookups' to 'true'. For other versions, remove the JndiLookup class from the classpath.",
  "notes": "Commonly referred to as 'Log4Shell'. Because this library is embedded in thousands of third-party enterprise applications and cloud services, the actual list of affected downstream products is extremely large. Note that early mitigations like 'formatMsgNoLookups' were found to be incomplete in certain non-default configurations, so upgrading remains the only fully robust fix.",
  "confidence_0_100": 100
}

  "notes": "Commonly referred to as Log4Shell. Setting the system property 'log4j2.formatMsgNoLookups' to 'true' was previously recommended as a mitigation for version 2.10 to 2.14.1, but this was later found to be insufficient in certain configurations (leading to CVE-2021-45046), making upgrading the preferred solution.",
  "confidence_0_100": 100
}
